target_customer: Companies whose employees build AI agents and automations, with IT controlling access and spend (customers named include Shopify, Ramp, Gusto, Samsara, Instacart, Opendoor)
problem: Non-technical employees want to automate work with AI but lack tools, while IT needs governance over models, data and spend.
business_model: SaaS subscription with usage credits, enterprise plans
product_category: AI agent and workflow automation builder

founders.name: Max Brodeur-Urbas
education: McGill University (per secondary report, not opened primary)
founders.background_notes: Former Microsoft software engineer per TechCrunch.

founders.name: Rahul Behal
founders.background_notes: Named co-founder in TechCrunch Series A article; YC page lists only Max as founder.

competitors.name: Zapier
competitors.traction_then: Market leader with thousands of app integrations (own listing 8,000+ apps in 2026)

technical_complexity.rationale: Began as a UI wrapper over Auto-GPT, then needed a node-based canvas, many integrations and reliable LLM execution; standard engineering with some hard parts.

defensibility.rationale: Workflows and integrations create some lock-in, but large incumbents and many startups offer similar builders and models are interchangeable.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Zapier and others added AI features and OpenAI and others shipped agent tools; Gumloop kept growing and raised a Series B in March 2026.

market_need_then: In 2023 non-technical users in a Discord server wanted to use Auto-GPT without coding (TechCrunch). Interest in AI automation rose sharply with GPT-4.

branding.name_origin: Originally AgentHub. Renamed to Gumloop in 2024 because agent meant little to non-technical users, loop reflects repeating automations, and the founders wanted a free .com and .ai domain (company blog).
branding.domain_note: AgentHub used agenthub.dev, which signaled a developer-only product and caused 'not .com, .dev' confusion; Gumloop name chosen partly because .com and .ai were available (company blog, 2024).

identity.logo: Wordmark and mark described only in company assets; not verified in detail

branding.brand_signature: Gumloop name itself, a playful memorable coinage

rebrands.why: Agent was jargon, .dev domain confused users, wanted .com and .ai

branding.community_and_virality: Company runs a blog and Handbook and publishes comparison pages; no sourced evidence of merch or fan accounts.

brand_strength.rationale: Distinctive name chosen deliberately after a rebrand with clear reasons; no mascot or large community evidence found.

pivots.from: AgentHub, a drag-and-drop automation platform wrapping Auto-GPT
pivots.why: Rebrand and broadening to non-technical users

pivots.to: Multiplayer AI agent builder with IT controls
pivots.why: Company repositioned toward enterprise agents; company says it is not a visual workflow builder

outcome_analysis: Gumloop grew from a Vancouver side project into a YC W24 company, then raised a 3.1M seed in July 2024, a 17M Series A in January 2025 and a 50M Series B led by Benchmark in March 2026. Success came from riding the AI automation wave, a deliberate rename, fast shipping and enterprise customers. No shutdown or acquisition news exists.
notes: Series A reported as 24.5M by BetaKit and Techcouver, likely CAD; company blog says 17M USD. Total raised figures conflict across aggregators (20M, 70M, 120M). Competitors are cited from 2025 sources describing the market, not strictly dated to the batch. McGill education comes from a secondary search summary, not an opened primary page, so treat as unverified.
